textbookText: 7. A person is trying to lift a stone of 500 N keeping it on the smaller piston of a hydraulic machine by applying a force on the larger piston. What suggestion would you give him/her so that he/she can lift the load easily? Explain, with an appropriate figure, the process of increasing the force in the hydraulic machine. Ans:- A person trying to lift a 500 N stone using a hydraulic machine should place the stone on the larger piston and apply effort on the smaller piston. This is because, according to Pascal’s law, pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally in all directions. When a small force is applied on the smaller piston, the same pressure acts on the larger piston, but because its area is greater, it produces a much larger lifting force. Thus, even a small effort can raise a heavy load. In a hydraulic system, the mechanical advantage increases when the ratio of the area of the large piston to the area of the small piston is high. This means the person should use a smaller input piston, ensure the system is filled with fluid without air bubbles, and apply steady pressure for smooth lifting. This setup allows the hydraulic machine to multiply force effectively and lift the stone with ease. 8. Calculate the upthrust acting on the object in situations b and c shown in the figure. Mention the cause for the occurrence of different upthrusts under these two situations. (Ans: 10 N, 6 N) Ans:- Given Weight of the object on air = 20N In situation a, weight of the object on liquid = 10N Upthrust acting on the object in situation a = Weight of the object on air - weight of the object on liquid

= 20N – 10N = 10N In situation b, weight of the object on liquid = 14N Upthrust acting on the object in situation b = Weight of the object on air - weight of the object on liquid = 20N – 14N = 6N The varying upthrusts experienced by the object in the two situations—partial and full submersion—are fundamentally caused by the difference in the volume of the object submerged in the liquid. According to Archimedes' Principle, the upthrust (buoyant force) is directly proportional to the weight of the fluid displaced; since the density of the fluid remains constant, the upthrust is solely determined by the volume of the object that is below the water line. In the case of partial submersion, only a fraction of the object's volume displaces water, resulting in a smaller upthrust, whereas in full submersion, the object displaces the maximum possible volume of water (equal to its total volume), thereby experiencing the maximum upthrust. 9. In the figure, a sample of a hydraulic machine constructed by using syringes is shown. How much force is to be applied through syringe B to balance the force on syringe A? (Ans: 200 N) Ans:- let the small piston is 1 and large piston is 2 then, Force exerted by piston 1 (F1) = 20N Area of piston 1 (A1) = 0.5 cm² Force exerted by piston 2 (F2) = ? Area of piston 2 (A2) = 5 cm² then using Pascal’s Principle 𝐹1 = 𝐹2 𝐴1 𝐴2 or, 20N 0.5 cm² = 𝐹2 5 cm² or, 𝐹2 = 5 cm²∗ 20N 0.5 cm² = 200N The force to be applied through syringe B to balance the 20N force on syringe A is 200 N. 10. Pressure of 30000 Pa is generated in the liquid of a hydraulic lift. If the cross-sectional area of the piston used to lift a weight is 0.1 m², how much load can it lift? (Ans: 3000 N ) Ans:- Given, Pressure (P) = 30000 Pa Area (A) = 0.1 m² Force (F) = ? Now we know that, F= P * A = 30000 * 0.1N = 3000N Therefore 3000N load can it lift. ***
